extraction_scope: Worker-6 final mechanism adjudication bounded to primary model-membrane evidence; introduction-only protein/DNA mechanisms are not promoted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Polydim-I changes conformation in membrane-mimetic environments and shows increased helical contribution in TFE/SDS/AZO contexts relative to buffer.
mechanism_claims.limitations: These assays support peptide structure in model environments, not an organism-specific killing pathway by themselves.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Polydim-I forms channel-like conductive pores in anionic asolectin lipid bilayers under electrophysiology conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct evidence is from artificial lipid bilayers; bacterial membrane lysis remains inferred from model-membrane behavior and antimicrobial phenotype.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Polydim-I antimicrobial phenotype against ATCC and MDR bacteria
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper interprets membrane destabilization/pore formation as a probable, non-exclusive antibacterial mode of action based on model-membrane interaction and pore data.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct bacterial inner-membrane permeability assay, receptor assay, DNA synthesis assay, or protein synthesis assay is reported for this paper.
